column1: # Help texts captured from real tools, chosen to represent the shapes the help-text
# reader meets rather than as a sample.
# Columns, separated by tabs: the file is help-<name>.txt; outcome is the class
# tests/test_corpus.py asserts, one of usage-not-found, degraded or parsed; stream
# is where the command writes its help; version is the tool's at capture time;
# command is run by capture.py, which also pins the environment; shape says what
# the reader makes of the file and why.  Captured on macOS 26.6.2, with the bin
# directory of the cnvkit conda environment first on PATH and that of the dev
# environment second, which puts their samtools, htslib, wgsim and zstd ahead of any
# others and the cnvkit environment's miniwdl 1.14.2 ahead of the dev one's 1.15.0.

column6: Cobra heading USAGE, without a colon
two usage: markers in one docstring
the options block documents -o twice, as -o OUTPUT and the dictionary builder's -o NAME, and the synopsis names -o, so parse_pattern raises and the positionals are lost while the options survive
the second value of -e and the list after the value of -c are read as one positional; the wrapped synopsis line opening with -c is synopsis, not an option entry
[OPTIONS] read as a positional; the options block directly under the synopsis ends it
positionals recovered cleanly once the brackets argparse writes around an optional value, as in [-p [PROCESSES]], are removed on a second reading
argparse's WDL_URI [WDL_URI ...] read as two positionals

[OPTIONS] read as a positional; -a and -b, which the options block omits, take the placeholders the synopsis writes after them; -f and -F, whose descriptions name the value's type, take a value, while options whose value only prose describes, such as -g and -iobuf, read as switches
positionals recovered cleanly; the options block directly under the synopsis ends it
no options block, so the value of -D is read as a positional
FILES [FILES ...] read as two positionals, while -n NORMAL [NORMAL ...] is one option taking a list; a wrapped line opening with --normal is prose, and its [Default: polish] is --normalize-method's

GNU's or: continues the synopsis; both alternatives begin samtools merge and align by position, so -o takes <out.bam> in the first while the second's <out.bam> shares the first slot with <in1.bam> ...
the or: alternative begins git show, so a warning names git log as the command wrapped and <object>... shares the slot of <revision-range>; <options> and -- are read as positionals
